output.summary: The run is marked VALID, but the deterministic policy verdict is NO_VERDICT with INCOMPLETE coverage (reasons: RESOURCE_GAPS, MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS). The reference window passed (business PASS, resource PASS; latency p95=68ms <= 200ms; compute-limit and database-limit SLA checks PASS). In the workload-01 window the latency business rule PASSed, but the database-limit SLA check was NO_VERDICT because 10 of 180 system-db-work cells were missing, so that window and the run as a whole are NO_VERDICT, not PASS. All nine resource-versus-latency correlation pairs are INSUFFICIENT_DATA with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED because target rate, achieved rate, latency, and resource series were essentially constant and the requested control target-request-rate was dropped; the five anomaly checks reported NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE under ZERO_MAD. Clock alignment was not verified by core, so no temporal ordering is supported. The evidence supports rerunning with complete system-db-work telemetry and verified clocks, and using a workload with load variation before any correlation or sensitivity conclusions.

hypotheses.observation: The workload-01 window summary reports resource_verdict NO_VERDICT and verdict NO_VERDICT even though the latency policy check for that window is PASS (observed response time p95 = 68ms).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The database-limit SLA rule could not be evaluated for workload-01 because the system-db-work series had 10 missing cells out of 180 (reason RESOURCE_GAPS) and the policy check is NO_VERDICT with reason MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS; missing resource cells block a resource verdict for that window and therefore the run-level verdict.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the collection path for the system-db-work series in the workload-01 window (epoch range 1704067320000-1704067500000) to find why 10 cells were missing, fix the gap, and rerun so the database-limit rule is actually evaluated.

hypotheses.observation: All nine correlation pairs in workload-01 (e.g., association-01 and association-02) are INSUFFICIENT_DATA with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED; the engine dropped the requested control target-request-rate and reports reasons including NO_RANK_VARIATION, CONSTANT_CONTROL, RESOURCE_DELTA_BELOW_MINIMUM, and LOAD_DELTA_BELOW_MINIMUM; all headline selections are UNAVAILABLE (PAIR_NOT_EVALUABLE).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: During workload-01, the target and achieved generator rates were constant at 80 requests/s, latency was constant at 68ms, and every evaluated resource series was constant, so there was no variation for the association analysis to estimate any relationship.
hypotheses.recommended_check: If association or sensitivity estimates are wanted, rerun with a controlled load profile containing ramps or steps in target rate so that load, latency, and resource series vary enough for the correlation engine to evaluate.

hypotheses.observation: The resource binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core, and the correlation pairs report LAG_NOT_EVALUABLE.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The time relationship between metric sources has not been verified by the core analysis, so no lead/lag or temporal ordering between load, latency, and resource series can be inferred from this evidence.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock synchronization across all telemetry sources before drawing any temporal conclusions from these series.

hypotheses.observation: The overall and per-transaction metric summaries list latency p50 = p95 = p99 = max = 68ms with 0 errors over 24000 samples, and both window summaries also report latency max = p99 = p95 = p50 = 68ms.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Identical values across all latency quantiles suggest coarse aggregation or rounding in the reported latency metric rather than a natural response-time distribution; the evidence does not demonstrate that every request took exactly 68ms.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the raw per-sample latency values in the source JTL/CSV data to verify the resolution and distribution behind the 68ms figures.

hypotheses.observation: The diagnostic summary reports anomalies_tested = 5 with episodes_reported = 0, and each anomaly check status is NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE with reason ZERO_MAD.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The series are constant with zero median absolute deviation, so the anomaly detector could not establish a baseline spread; zero reported episodes therefore does not prove stability or absence of change.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Review the raw series directly and, if material-change detection is needed, use a workload with variation rather than relying on ZERO_MAD-based NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE results.

hypotheses.observation: The reference window is PASS (business PASS and resource PASS), the run is VALID, yet the run-level policy verdict is NO_VERDICT with analysis coverage INCOMPLETE.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A PASS on the earlier reference window does not carry to the run because the later workload-01 window is NO_VERDICT; business latency rules passed in both windows, and the incomplete part is resource evaluation, so the run is inconclusive rather than failed or passed.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Treat this run as inconclusive; rerun with complete resource telemetry to obtain a definitive verdict, and do not report the run as PASS based on the reference window alone.

recommendations.action: Rerun the test with complete system-db-work telemetry for the workload-01 window and verified clock alignment so the database-limit SLA rule can be evaluated.
recommendations.rationale: The only barrier to a resource verdict in workload-01 is the database-limit check being NO_VERDICT due to MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS; with complete cells, the window and possibly the run verdict could be determined.

recommendations.action: Investigate why 10 of 180 system-db-work cells were missing in workload-01 (epoch range 1704067320000-1704067500000) before rerunning.
recommendations.rationale: The evidence reports RESOURCE_GAPS with missing_cells = 10 for db_work but does not state why; identifying the cause (collector, scrape interval, or export pipeline) prevents the same gap from recurring.

recommendations.action: Verify clock synchronization across metric sources.
recommendations.rationale: Clock alignment is not_verified_by_core, so temporal ordering and lead/lag claims about these series are unsupported until clocks are confirmed.

recommendations.action: Run a workload with controlled load variation (ramps or steps) if association or sensitivity estimates are wanted.
recommendations.rationale: Every correlation pair was INSUFFICIENT_DATA because target rate, achieved rate, latency, and resource series were constant and the requested control was dropped; variation is required to estimate any association.

recommendations.action: Keep the run-level verdict reported as NO_VERDICT and do not mark the run as PASS based on the reference window.
recommendations.rationale: The reference window PASS does not override the workload-01 NO_VERDICT resource evaluation; business latency PASS alone does not yield a full window or run verdict.

caveats: The deterministic verdict is NO_VERDICT; the reference window's PASS must not be read as a run-level PASS.

analysis_coverage is INCOMPLETE with reasons RESOURCE_GAPS and MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS; the database-limit rule for workload-01 was not evaluated, and the reason for the 10 missing system-db-work cells is not provided in the evidence.
clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core, so no lead/lag or temporal causal ordering between the series is supported.
All correlation pairs are INSUFFICIENT_DATA with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED; this means no association was estimated, not that no association exists.
Anomaly checks ran under ZERO_MAD and reported 0 episodes; this does not prove stability, spare capacity, or absence of a problem.

Flat or low constant values (e.g., system-cpu-work at 0.2, system-db-work at 0.8 in the reference window, cpu-service-quota at 1) do not by themselves prove that resources have spare capacity or that the system is unloaded; the database-limit check was not evaluated in workload-01.

Overall sample_count 24000 and window sample counts 9600 (reference) and 14400 (workload-01) cover different windows and scopes, so they are not directly comparable and are not inconsistent by that fact alone.
